answer_summary.ion_591_given_example: [E + H]+  ((590 + 1)/1 = 591; planted example from answer sheet A6-2, verifies the proton-attachment convention and integer masses)
answer_summary.ion_783: [3E + C48 + 3H]3+  ((3*590 + 576 + 3)/3 = 2349/3 = 783) — triply protonated aggregate of three macrocycles E (C40H34N2O3) with one intact cyclo[48]carbon; uniquely determined (ion783_unique)
answer_summary.ion_879: [2E + C48 + 2H]2+  ((2*590 + 576 + 2)/2 = 1758/2 = 879) — doubly protonated 2:1 aggregate of E with C48; uniquely determined (ion879_unique)
answer_summary.ion_1174: [3E + C48 + 2H]2+  ((3*590 + 576 + 2)/2 = 2348/2 = 1174) — doubly protonated 3:1 aggregate of E with C48; unique at charge state 2 (ion1174_unique_at_charge_two). Residual integer-m/z ambiguity with [C48 + E + 8H]+ (576+590+8 = 1174) is explicitly reported; the singly charged 8-proton 1:1 aggregate is chemically unreasonable (only two basic N atoms) and inconsistent with the multiply protonated aggregate pattern forced by 783 and 879.

assumptions: Integer atomic masses as instructed by 6.4: H = 1, C = 12, N = 14, O = 16 (trusted general law level: standard integer isotope masses).
Problem-printed molecular formulae: macrocycle E = C40H34N2O3 (printed under structure E on Q6-2; M = 590) and cyclo[48]carbon = C48 (M = 576) — actual problem inputs, not derived.

Positive-mode electrospray ionization by proton attachment only, as anchored by the planted example [E + H]+ at m/z 591 on answer sheet A6-2 (the alternative [E - H]- would give 589, not 591, so the example itself discriminates).
No fragmentation (problem statement): each ion is an integer combination of intact E and C48 molecules plus protons.

Uniqueness domains used in the Lean theorems are not arbitrary bounds: per-field finite bounds are proved from the mass equation by omega; the qualitative restrictions (charge state z <= 3, at most z protons, at most one C48 ring) reflect the electrospray aggregation window of the sample (one catenated cyclocarbon per catenane) and are stated explicitly in each theorem.
source_gaps: m/z 1174 is not uniquely determined by integer m/z arithmetic alone: the formal alternative [C48 + E + 8H]+ (z = 1, mass 1174) satisfies the same integer data and the same proton-attachment convention. The problem never states the charge state, and no isotope-resolution information exists at integer accuracy. The planted/chemically reasonable answer [3E + C48 + 2H]2+ is adopted and its uniqueness at z = 2 is proved; the ambiguity is recorded here and in answer.md (and witnessed constructively by IChO2026T6A4.catenane_octaprotonated_mz) instead of being assumed away.
No textbook-scale ambiguity exists for 783 and 879: both are proved unique within the chemically motivated candidate space.
